key_insight: Universal quantum state purification obeys a quantitative magic–fidelity tradeoff: higher target fidelity at fixed success probability requires more nonstabilizer resources.
engineering_relevance: This gives a resource-law perspective for designing error-mitigation and fault-tolerant protocols, helping estimate how much quantum magic is needed to improve noisy-state preparation.
method: Prove an exact linear mana law for two-copy purification in odd dimensions.
Derive a two-sided linear robustness law for multi-qubit systems, exact for a single qubit.
Construct an explicit successful purification map to expose the tradeoff between resource cost, success probability, and fidelity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact analytic laws, including exact results in odd dimensions and a single-qubit case, rather than empirical benchmarking data.
watch_item: The strongest exact results are dimension- and system-dependent, so extending the law to arbitrary higher-dimensional or many-body settings may require additional assumptions or new proofs.
paper_title: A Nonstabilizerness Resource Law for Universal Quantum State Purification
